## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `finished_at` column needs fixing before merge because it holds a start timestamp; this is the Critical finding about running processes.

## Changes
This pull request adds a `finished_at` column to the `processes` current-state model. The column is derived from the latest event's `occurred_at` and is documented in `models/schema.yml`. The pull request also adds a one-line `review.txt` at the repository root.

## Critical
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — Stop reporting start time as finished_at — For process 20, whose latest event is `'started'` at `2026-01-01T00:01:00Z`, `finished_at` gets that start time even though the process is still running. The expression `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end` fills the column only for started processes, and the `event_type` check in `sources/process_events.sql:4` allows no finishing event. — Consumers of `processes` will treat every running process as finished at its start time. — Fix: Decide which event type marks completion, add it to the source constraint if needed, and fill `finished_at` only from that event, or rename the column to `started_at` if a start time is what you meant.

## Important
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Correct the documented NULL meaning of finished_at — Process 30 was started (event 3) and then cleared (event 4), yet it gets `finished_at` NULL, which contradicts "NULL means the process has never been started." The code returns a value only when the latest event is `'started'`, so any started process that later moved to another state gets NULL. — Analysts who rely on the schema catalog will misclassify cleared processes as never started.
